meta.title: Marketing Analytics Decision Brief
meta.methodology: 365-day primary attribution with 30/90/180/365-day sensitivity; resolved-outcome win rates; cohort maturity controls

scope: ICP, account coverage, 6sense, email, creative, and budget strategy
guardrails: Answer only questions related to this dashboard, marketing analytics, ABM strategy, attribution, ROI, pipeline quality, ICP, 6sense, email, creative, budget testing, data quality, or presenting the findings.
If a user asks about unrelated topics, politely redirect to dashboard and marketing questions.
Do not invent new numbers. Use the facts below and clearly label directional assumptions.
Attribution and ROI are planning signals, not proof of causality.

recommendation.headline: Targeted growth, not blanket budget expansion.
actions: Protect pipeline quality by reviewing ICP and qualification before scaling broad top-of-funnel volume.
Expand coverage to unreached strong-fit CRM account domains.
Start with email coverage, then test a 6sense overlay with a holdout before scaling.
Use sourced and influenced attribution together, with sourced as conservative credit and influenced as journey context.
Run holdout or phased tests to measure incremental lift before large budget changes.

caveats: Attribution is directional and does not prove causality.
Attribution coverage changes with lookback; the primary view uses 365 days and sensitivity checks use 30, 90, 180, and 365 days.
Spend ROI only covers channels with reliable tracked spend.
Low-volume channels and segments can be unstable.
Web traffic is partially anonymous unless matched to account domains.
A calendar-only win-probability baseline was withdrawn after a near-chance holdout; no deal scores are published.
The email file is an engagement-event log; send-based open and click rates cannot be calculated.
A large share of won opportunities has zero amount, so won revenue and revenue ROI are understated.

marketing_concepts.abm: ABM focuses sales and marketing on a defined CRM account universe instead of broad demand generation.
marketing_concepts.icp: ICP defines the accounts most worth pursuing using profile fit, segment, industry, win rate, and deal size.
marketing_concepts.sourced_vs_influenced: Sourced is conservative CRM origin credit; influenced is journey context for the subset of opportunities linked to eligible pre-opportunity touches.
marketing_concepts.holdout_test: Use treatment and holdout groups to measure whether coverage expansion creates incremental meetings, opportunities, pipeline, and win-rate quality.

rows.Why: Closed-deal win rate moved from 38% to 22% across cohorts at least 80% resolved.
rows.Next step: Run a quarterly ICP and qualification review before scaling volume.

rows.Why: 67.7% of CRM account domains are unreached by tracked email or 6sense.
rows.Next step: Define exposure before future outcomes; exclude customers and active pipeline, then randomize eligible strong-fit domains to treatment and holdout.

rows.Why: 684 opportunities link to classified marketing touches; 11.9% of won deals are covered.
rows.Next step: Use journey models for hypothesis generation, then validate lift with holdouts.

rows.Recommendation: Expand coverage to unreached CRM account domains.
rows.Why We Believe It: 3,232 CRM account domains are unreached, and 2024 reached groups show higher all-history opportunity prevalence; time ordering and selection prevent a conversion or lift claim.
rows.What To Test Next: Exclude existing customers and active pipeline; define exposure before future opportunity outcomes, then compare eligible strong-fit domains with a randomized holdout.

rows.Why We Believe It: Journey and attribution patterns show email often starts conversations while 6sense appears later in the path.
rows.What To Test Next: Trigger display frequency after email engagement and measure lift in meetings, opportunities, pipeline, and win rate.

rows.Why We Believe It: Cohort analysis shows pipeline growth alongside a mature-cohort closed-win-rate move from 38% to 22%.
rows.What To Test Next: Track win rate, stage conversion, and disqualification reasons by source and profile fit.

rows.Recommendation: Reserve budget for a causal measurement plan.
rows.Why We Believe It: Only two paid channels have tracked spend, one has a single opportunity, and neither has recorded won revenue.
rows.What To Test Next: Use a budget-neutral holdout and pre-register incremental qualified pipeline as the decision metric.

rows.Action: Coverage: test email-first reach with a randomized holdout after customer and active-pipeline exclusions.
rows.Why: Email-only accounts show a 45.6% historical opportunity prevalence and both-channel accounts show 42.4%, compared with 17.6% for unreached accounts.
rows.Measure Success With: Future opportunity creation after assigned exposure, qualified pipeline and randomized treatment-minus-holdout lift; current prevalence is not the baseline.

rows.Action: Pipeline quality: tighten ICP and qualification criteria.
rows.Why: Quarterly pipeline is rising while closed-deal win rate moved from 38% to 22%.
rows.Measure Success With: Win rate, stage conversion, disqualification reasons.

rows.Action: Attribution reporting: report sourced and influenced side by side.
rows.Why: Sourced pipeline is $4.2M, while influenced pipeline is $6.4M.
rows.Measure Success With: Sourced pipeline, influenced pipeline, influenced won revenue.

rows.Action: Marketing conversion: fix lead-to-opportunity qualification before adding marketing-sourced volume.
rows.Why: Marketing-sourced acquisition has the lowest resolved win rate of any lead-source group in 2023–24; see the decision brief, slide main-06.
rows.Measure Success With: Marketing-sourced resolved win rate and won amount per opportunity, by quarter, against referral.

rows.Action: Creative: test engagement patterns within matched platform/audience conditions.
rows.Why: CTR is descriptive and audience/delivery/creative attributes are confounded; no causal creative effect is identified.
rows.Measure Success With: Qualified-opportunity outcomes, delivery coverage and cost guardrails; CTR is a supporting diagnostic.

rows.What The Evaluator Should See: Eight raw sources are cleaned, deduplicated, normalized by domain, and rebuilt through reproducible scripts.
Won revenue, attribution, funnel, and dashboard artifacts are checked for consistency before presentation.
The story is focused: marketing influence is broader than source credit, but growth must protect quality.
The default page prioritizes decision-critical charts; deeper charts are available but not forced.
